author.role: Implementation author documenting missing prerequisites; not an independent source review

current_transition_gate: Await each already declared fresh normal/controller_loss case's own accepted exact prelaunch and single actual dispatch; failed or partial outcomes remain consumed, never retry/fallback.
Independently audit actual raw streams, identities, inherited pipe closures, ARM/ACK order, symbolic signal count, pidfd and matching parent wait facts. CI fixture success is not MS host success.

Publish/integrate the observed result honestly before using it as context for a new source stage. Successful fixed cases would establish only those bounded owned direct-worker cases, not production containment.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: Current guard is the sole worker wait parent; its loss leaves no independently proven worker termination/adoption/reap. Worker self-expiry is a code path, not observed recovery.
concrete_missing_prerequisites.required_evidence: A separate live guardian with anchored worker pidfd and an independently reviewed adoption/wait protocol must survive deliberately induced owned guard loss, verify original PID birth/UID/boot/nonce, perform only authorized cleanup and independently observe termination/reap.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: Current logical-controller loss assumes coordinator and guard remain alive. Coordinator or Python observer loss does not yield a complete independently observed report or bounded cleanup proof.
concrete_missing_prerequisites.required_evidence: Loss-surviving ownership transfer and independent terminal observer, with no required final write from the dead role; test each deliberate owned loss boundary and preserve partial/unknown outcomes rather than claiming host-loss recovery.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: The current worker never execs or forks further descendants. One fixed tree is not an arbitrary-descendant controller, and PID/PPID equality alone cannot cover reparenting, FD handoff, late forks or exec transitions.
concrete_missing_prerequisites.required_evidence: Review an explicit allowed exec/source/argv closure and membership protocol before running another fixed helper that execs or forks. Track each fresh member's boot/UID/birth/parent/nonce and anchored pidfd, reject untracked membership, and verify controlled reparenting/adoption independently. A bounded fixture remains a fixture; any production child model must declare and cover its actual process behavior.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: Current fourteen-second CPU fixture has no production controller/guard adapter, full source/runtime ownership interface or 4500s work plus1500s restoration protocol.
concrete_missing_prerequisites.required_evidence: Separate reviewed/pushed/integrated operational closure with checked ownership before launch and critical actions, native guard-loss behavior, typed clock/identity/source errors, bounded independent cleanup and exact release conditions. Keep old native/Python APIs and --execute refusals intact; no shim or success boolean can supply this interface.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: No controlled model-bearing child has imported exact scientificA/nativeA plus new operational closure, loaded pinned weights or observed the frozen settings/tensors/gradients.

Observe actual BF16 frozen base, FP32 trainables, adapter/head state, settings and original first-step accumulated/clipped gradient hook without added forward/backward or heldout tuning. Do not substitute report/main commits for pinned scientificA/nativeA.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: Current full76 package metadata/positions/pipcheck, executable/source/data/weight identity and Torch/native/CUDA numerical runtime observations remain unverified.

concrete_missing_prerequisites.missing: CPU markers/pidfds do not grant GPU ownership, reserve foreign cards, evacuate CUDA memory or establish recoverable original optimizer state.

smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.proposal: One independently reviewed loss-surviving guardian/adoption fixture, initially one fixed non-model worker and no exec, services or foreign processes.
smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.first_concrete_gap: Give a separate live owned guardian an anchored worker descriptor before arming, then deliberately lose the worker's current guard. Use reviewed symbolic Linux headers/interfaces for ownership transfer and controlled subreaper/adoption as needed, and independently verify the same original worker's termination and the correct surviving parent's wait outcome.
smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.second_case_in_same_reviewed_architectur: After the guard-loss protocol is explicit, deliberately lose the owned coordinator while the separate guardian survives; this exercises surviving ownership and evidence collection rather than another presence probe.
smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.design_must_settle: Exact process/FD layout, guardian survival assumption, authorized member handoff, PPID transition policy, packet/source/deadline binding and independent exit observation. No external PID, arbitrary command, guessed constants or current product reuse.
smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.success_limit: Only the tested fixed tree and deliberate owned loss boundaries. Guardian/host loss, arbitrary descendants, exec/model bridge, production deadlines, GPU lease and foreign restoration remain open.
smallest_useful_next_CPU_design.reason_to_choose_it: It closes the precise current single-parent cleanup/evidence gap and provides an ownership interface the later controlled runtime/model child can actually use.

sequencing: This note creates no new source, nonce, request, host declaration or dispatch. Begin a later normal source branch only after current observed results are reviewed and integrated.

Independent design and meaningful portable/real Linux fixtures precede implementation acceptance; new code then needs commit/push, independent source/committed/CI review, attached PR, all latest exact-head CI and actual main integration.
Only afterward may a separate fresh exact-prelaunch review bind a new non-model host episode. Old controller, PID, source-proof, attempt, output, marker and argv remain permanently consumed.

A validated loss-surviving CPU ownership interface is a prerequisite for a separate controlled runtime/model bridge; every later model/GPU step still needs its own frozen source/resource/restoration evidence.
